**Reasoning:**

**High-confidence catchable bugs (85%+):**
- Input type validation (wrong `frame` or non-bool `copy`)
- Missing null mask handling entirely (would corrupt output)
- Wrong dtype assignments (Int64Dtype, BooleanDtype, StringDtype)
- Missing column names or order
- Empty frame crashes
- Missing metadata restoration

**Medium-confidence catchable bugs (60-80%):**
- Specific null positions wrong (depends on test data design)
- Partial null mask handling (only some paths affected)
- Column name/dtype mismatches that visible in output

**Hard-to-catch bugs (20-40%):**
- Copy parameter behavior changes (can't verify zero-copy externally)
- Mask.any() condition modifications (only break specific null+copy combinations)
- Object aliasing issues (require checking numpy buffer ownership)
- Subtle dtype coercion differences (Int64Dtype vs pandas defaults)

**Why 72% and not higher:** The function has several internal optimization paths (especially FLOAT64's `if copy or mask.any()`) where a bug might only fail when specific combinations of nulls + copy parameter are used. Without dynamically exploring the full state space during one test run, some edge-case bugs could slip through. The public API also doesn't expose enough detail to verify zero-copy guarantees.
